title: Entropy throttle release notes & scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the entropy-throttle release. This is a working doc: notes, small checklists, command snippets and open questions. Not final runbook.

Context:
- Feature: entropy-throttle (dynamic traffic damping based on rolling instability score).
- Goal: soft-cap high-variance models during region-level spikes so tail latency and error budget hold.
- Deployment mode: staged canary -> regional ramp -> global flip.

High-level rollout plan (sketch):
1) Canary day 0: internal stable cohort only (team + dogfood). 2% traffic, 4h heat-check window.
2) Canary day 1: broaden to beta clients (opt-in SDK flag). 5% traffic, 6h window.
3) Region ramp: EU-west then NA-east then AP-south. Increment by +10% every 12h if metrics good.
4) Global baseline: 50% for 48h, then decide full flip.

Heat-check metrics (live dashboards):
- p99 latency (inference): baseline + tolerance 50ms. Fail if >120ms absolute or +30% relative.
- error rate (5xx + model-detected-failures): fail if >0.8% absolute or +3x baseline.
- token-cost / request: monitor for >15% uplift (indicates degraded model behavior).
- stability score (new): 3-min rolling, fail if >0.7 for 10m.
- client error feedback: Slack channel #stability-alerts (tag relevant PMs).

Quick checklist before canary (preflight):
- [ ] Feature flag created: ff/entropy-throttle (verified on staging).
- [ ] Canary image built and hashed: sha256:fa12... (store in release notes).
- [ ] Telemetry hooks enabled: metrics name prefix = infra.entropy.*
- [ ] Alerting: create temporary PagerDuty policy for the window (INF-ROTATION).
- [ ] Run smoke tests (basic generation, rerank, streaming).
- [ ] Data retention: ensure logs exported to s3://redwood-release-logs/entropy/2026-02.
- [ ] Canary cohort list updated (internal-only user ids uploaded).

Commands / snippets I use frequently:
- Pin model in route: curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/routes/pin -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"rf-3b-v2","version":"2026-02-rc1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Unpin: curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/routes/unpin -d '{"route":"/v1/generate"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Flip traffic using router: rbctl set-weight --route /v1/generate --target=entropy-throttle --pct=5 --commit-msg "canary 5%"
- Quick kql for request failures: errors | where timestamp > ago(15m) and route == "/v1/generate" and status_code >= 500 | summarize count() by error_type
- Stability score query (approx): telemetry | where metric == "stability_score" and region == "eu-west" | summarize avg(value) by bin(1m)

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- any 3x spike in 5xx within 15m OR sustained p99 > 150ms for 20m => immediate rollback to previous config and pin previous model.
- if token cost > +25% over baseline for 2h => pause rollout and investigate.
- unexplained client errors (>=3 high-severity client tickets within window) => halt.

Safety knobs and mitigations:
- fallback variant: route fallback to rf-3b-v2-quant (lower-cost) configured in router with graceful degrade.
- autonomous throttle: if stability_score > 0.85 trigger automatic soft-throttle (reduce pct by 50%).
- canary timebox: if any critical alerts, we have 30m to rollback before PD escalation.

Notes on cohort composition:
- internal: 12 service accounts (team/dev), not business-critical.
- beta clients: 3 external customers agreed to opt-in (IDs listed in SSM param /release/canaries/beta).
- warmup: pre-warm KV caches for each canary client with a 30m synthetic traffic generator.

Open questions / TODOs (my quick brain dump):
- Should we hold EU ramp 24h longer because of typical traffic patterns? (ask product on Thu)
- How to surface cost-impacts to customers in console while opt-in? Quick UX tick? (ping UX)
- Confirm if HSM-backed KMS rotation scheduled in same week (if so, avoid full flip).
- Add synthetic test that intentionally injects high-entropy prompts to exercise throttle logic.

Post-mortem items (if failure):
- capture full trace for first 120s of incident and preserve at s3://redwood-incidents/entropy/<timestamp>
- run automated evaluation harness against golden prompt set to check for latent quality regressions.

Communication plan (short):
- Canary start: announce in #deploys with runbook link and PD roster.
- On incidents: post periodic updates every 15m, escalate to ENG-LEAD if >30m unresolved.
- Post-success: send summary to #releases and product mailing list with link to cost/latency dashboard.

Quick log of today (seed notes):
- 2026-02-09 09:12 - built canary image, smoke tests passed locally.
- 2026-02-09 09:35 - enabled telemetry in staging; dashboard panel created (entropy throttle view).
- 2026-02-10 17:00 - ran warmup generator against eu-west; caches warmed ~95%, synthetic p99 42ms.

Personal heuristics (why this matters):
- We often see small but persistent regressed tails surface only after full ramp. Damping early reduces blast radius.
- Keep canaries small but timebox them long enough to exercise hourly cron workloads (hence multi-day region ramps sometimes).

Scratch ideas for future improvements:
- per-client adaptive windows (clients with stable history get faster ramp).
- better visualization of token-cost deltas per route in console.
- auto-suggest batch sizes / kv cache TTLs based on observed sequence length distributions.

End of scratchpad.
Questions for next sync:
- Who will own PD rotation during the first EU ramp? (assign if not already)
- Are we ok with the current failure thresholds or do we want more conservative numbers?

-- LC
